final_report.summary: Investigated why af_engine.py suggestions are not appearing in the AtlasForge Activity log (dashboard chat feed). Root cause analysis revealed 5 bugs across af_engine.py and dashboard_v2.py. The primary cause is a startup pre-seeding bug in watch_chat() that marks all existing chat history as 'seen' without emitting to clients, permanently suppressing any suggestions that existed when the dashboard was last restarted. Secondary causes include: the watch_chat loop only scanning the last 10 messages (vs 30 in the REST endpoint), the _normalize_provider() function silently mapping 'system' to 'claude' (losing suggestion metadata), the legacy socket.js handler dropping metadata arguments, and a design mismatch where af_engine.py uses provider='system' which no dashboard handler recognizes.
key_achievements: Identified 5 distinct bugs causing the Activity log to not display suggestions
Traced the complete data flow from af_engine.py._save_recommendation() through chat_history.json to the dashboard WebSocket emission
Identified the primary root cause: watch_chat() startup pre-seeding marks all existing messages as 'seen' without emitting them
Identified secondary cause: watch_chat() only scans last 10 messages per poll cycle while the REST API returns 30
Identified provider normalization bug: 'system' provider silently becomes 'claude', losing suggestion styling
Identified legacy socket.js as missing metadata argument in addMessage() calls
Confirmed that the /api/chat-history REST polling fallback DOES show suggestions (explaining intermittent behavior)
challenges_overcome: Tracing indirect IPC through shared JSON file (chat_history.json) rather than direct function calls
Distinguishing between WebSocket push path and REST polling fallback path - both had different behaviors
Identifying the pre-seeding anti-pattern that marks messages as seen before emitting them
lessons_learned: Startup pre-seeding of deduplication sets should EMIT messages to clients before marking as seen, not after
All polling loops scanning recent history should use the same window size as the initial replay (30, not 10)
Provider/role normalization functions should preserve special values like 'system' rather than silently downgrading them
When two code paths (WebSocket push vs REST polling) handle the same data differently, the one with more filters will cause intermittent-looking bugs
The _normalize_provider guard should whitelist known providers but pass through unknown ones rather than mapping to a default
